key_insight: K-Bench introduces a clinically calibrated benchmark for testing how well large language models handle high-risk mental health conversations over multiple turns. It helps reveal whether models stay safe and appropriate when discussions involve suicide, self-harm, domestic violence, substance misuse, or low-risk scenarios.
problem_solved: LLMs are increasingly used for mental health support, but their behavior in realistic, evolving, high-risk conversations is not well understood. This paper addresses the lack of a rigorous, clinician-informed way to evaluate safety, consistency, and risk handling across different models.
method: Built K-Bench around 200 multi-turn mental health vignettes covering suicide, self-harm, domestic violence, substance misuse, and no-risk cases.
Calibrated the benchmark with clinicians to ensure the scenarios reflect high-risk, clinically meaningful conversation patterns.
Evaluated 125 model configurations spanning 33 base models from 14 providers to compare performance across safety-sensitive settings.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, K-Bench provides a practical standard for measuring whether LLMs are safe enough for mental health-related use cases. It can guide model selection, safety testing, and red-teaming for applications where mistakes can have serious consequences.
visual_elements: A benchmark pipeline diagram showing vignette creation, clinician calibration, and model evaluation.

paper_title: K-Bench: a clinically calibrated benchmark for evaluating large language models in high-risk mental health conversations
paper_authors: Laura M. Vowels, Matthew J. Vowels, Shivali Sharma, Apoorv Jha, Rehnuma Choudhury
